grammar_focus: 独立主格结构(名词 + being/分词,作状语:the only sign of life being a goat)、现在分词短语作状语(Taking a path …, Looking up …, Turning back …)、关系词 which/who 引导的修饰性从句、not only … but even … / be cut off from / be inaccessible to、形容词或分词后置修饰名词(a boatman fast asleep;houses built of mud bricks)(原创承载 NCE3 第三册 L48 考点·轻度软化措辞不换情节:旅行氛围叙事——夫妇周游巴尔干,误入一个沉默、戒备外人的偏僻山村,感到不受欢迎而折返;无暴力,把原文“敌意/怒视/警告”放缓为“戒备/注视/暗示”;美式化 traveled/gray/can)
scene: 在这个游客往来频繁的世界上,仍有成千上万个地方游客难以到达。人们总以为偏僻地方的村民热情好客。可那些不但与外国游客隔绝、甚至与本国同胞也隔绝的人,有可能对陌生人心存戒备。到真正偏僻的村庄去,很少是件轻松的事——我和妻子在一次周游巴尔干半岛时对此深有体会。我们在一座小镇上逗留了几天,参观了附近许多古老的教堂。这些教堂吸引了大量游客,不仅因为建筑风格奇特,还因为保存着大量完好的壁画。我们离开小镇的前一天,几辆满载游客的公共汽车涌进了镇子。这实在让我们受不了,于是我们决定用最后一天去乡间走走。走上一条出镇的小路,我们穿过几块农田,来到一片茂密的树林。原以为小路会突然到头,没想到它蜿蜒着穿过树林。我们在林中徒步走了两个多小时,来到一条深溪边。我们看得出小路在对岸继续延伸,却不知如何过溪。忽然,妻子发现岸边泊着一条小船,船上有个熟睡的船夫。我们轻轻把他唤醒,请他把我们摆渡过溪。他起初不大情愿,但经我们劝说,终于同意了。小路通向一个座落在陡峭山坡上的小村庄。那儿有一条散乱的、未经修筑的土路,两旁排列着一些矮小的农舍。即便在晴朗的蓝天下,村子也显得让人望而生畏,因为所有房子都用灰色土坯砌成。村子似乎无人居住,唯一的生命迹象,是拴在附近田里一棵树上的一只黑山羊。我们在田边一堵歪歪斜斜的木栅栏上坐下,打开几听沙丁鱼罐头,吃起了野外午餐。忽然,我注意到妻子神色不安。抬头一看,我发现我们已被一群衣衫褴褛的孩子围住,他们默默地看着我们吃东西。我们把食物递给他们,又和气地跟他们说话,他们却一动不动。我断定他们只是怕生。后来,我们沿村里的大街往下走时,身后跟着一队沉默的孩子。那个原本似乎空无一人的村子,忽然活了起来。一张张脸出现在窗口。穿着衬衫的男人站在自家门外注视着我们。裹着深色披巾的老妇人从门道里凝视我们。最奇怪的是,一点声音都听不见。毫无疑问,我们是不受欢迎的来客。我们不需要更多的暗示了。转身沿大街往回走,我们加快脚步,匆匆朝溪边赶去,盼着船夫还在那儿等着。

grammar_card.title: 独立主格结构 / 现在分词作状语 / which·who 关系从句 / not only…but even / 后置修饰
grammar_card.intro: ①独立主格结构:名词 + 分词(being/done/doing),作状语,补充说明主句:the only sign of life being a black goat。②现在分词短语放句首作状语:Taking a path …, Looking up …, Turning back …。③关系词 which(指物)/ who(指人)引导从句修饰前面的名词:a path which led …;children who were watching。④not only … but even …:不但…甚至…;be cut off from(与…隔绝)、be inaccessible to(难以到达)。⑤形容词或分词可放名词后修饰它:a boatman fast asleep;houses built of mud bricks;children in rags。

rows: 名词 + being/分词(独立主格)
the only sign of life being a goat
cut off not only from A but even from B
形容词/分词后置修饰名词

specialRules.rule: 独立主格里名词与分词是主动就用 -ing(sign … being),被动/完成就用过去分词(the meal finished）;它有自己的逻辑主语,与主句主语不同。
现在分词短语作状语时,其逻辑主语必须与主句主语一致（Looking up, I saw …,是 I 抬头）。
美式:traveled(英式 travelled)、gray(英式 grey)、can(英式 tin,指罐头)。本课已按美语写。

prelisten.q: Listen and answer — Why was the village silent?
options: The villagers were wary of strangers and quietly watched the unwelcome visitors
Everyone was taking an afternoon nap
A holiday had emptied the streets
The village had been abandoned long ago

passage: In this much-traveled world, there are still thousands of places that are inaccessible to tourists. We always assume that villagers in remote places are friendly and hospitable. But people who are cut off not only from foreign tourists, but even from their own countrymen, can be wary of strangers. Visits to really remote villages are seldom relaxing — as my wife and I discovered during a trip through the Balkans. We had spent several days in a small town and visited a number of old churches nearby. These attracted many visitors, for they were not only of great architectural interest but also contained a large number of beautifully preserved frescoes. On the day before we left, several busloads of tourists descended on the town. This was more than we could bear, so we decided to spend our last day exploring the countryside. Taking a path that led out of the town, we crossed a few fields until we came to a dense wood. We expected the path to end abruptly, but we found that it wound its way through the trees. We tramped through the wood for over two hours until we arrived at a deep stream. We could see that the path continued on the other side, but we had no idea how to get across. Suddenly my wife spotted a boat moored to the bank. In it there was a boatman fast asleep. We gently woke him up and asked him to ferry us to the other side. Though he was reluctant to do so at first, we eventually persuaded him to take us. The path led to a tiny village perched on the steep sides of a mountain. The place consisted of a straggling dirt road lined on either side by small houses. Even under a clear blue sky, the village looked unwelcoming, for all the houses were built of gray mud bricks. The village seemed deserted, the only sign of life being a black goat tied to a tree in a field nearby. Sitting down on a dilapidated wooden fence near the field, we opened a couple of cans of sardines and had a picnic lunch. All at once, I noticed that my wife seemed uneasy. Looking up, I saw that we were surrounded by children in rags who were watching us silently as we ate. We offered them food and spoke to them kindly, but they remained motionless. I concluded that they were simply shy of strangers. When we later walked down the main street of the village, we were followed by a silent procession of children. The village, which had seemed deserted, immediately came to life. Faces appeared at windows. Men in shirtsleeves stood outside their houses and stared at us. Old women in dark shawls peered at us from doorways. The strangest thing of all was that not a sound could be heard. There was no doubt that we were unwelcome visitors. We needed no further hint. Turning back down the main street, we quickened our pace and made our way rapidly toward the stream, where we hoped the boatman was still waiting.

stage5.stem: "The village was completely cut off ___ the outside world."(be cut off ___:与…隔绝,填介词)

stage5.stem: "A building that is old, broken and falling apart is ___."(“陈旧破烂的、倒塌的”用哪个词)
